records.name: 14, KING STREET
records.field_evidence: Early C19. Stucco. Three storeys, Three windows. Second floor windows in moulded architraves. First floor windows have cornices on console brackets. Ground floor has central bow window with pilasters and cornice. All sashes with glazing bars. Panelled door on right with rectangular fanlight. Sill band to first floor windows. Moulded eaves cornice. Slate roof.

records.name: 107 AND 109, HIGH CROSS STREET
records.field_evidence: Early C19 red brick front to probably C16 timber frame endcross-wing. Front: early C19 red brick, slate roof with gabled ends, wide eaves cornice with soffit brackets, two storeys, three widely spaced sashes with margin lights to first floor, without glazing bars, ground floor Victorian shop front with cornice and pilastered central doorway, carriageway on left. Cross-wing, originally said to be the Cross Keys Inn, timber frame mostly brick faced, but exposed timber framing to rear gable end. Arched brace roof with braced queen-post over tie-beam.

records.name: CLOCK TOWER
records.field_evidence: Clock Tower (Remains of the Original Midland Region Railway Station), Railway Terrace. Listed Building, Grade II.
